subject: Mutual Action Plan: Hosting mode & Region tiebreaker / next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Patel <sofia@mednex.com>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: Hosting mode & Region tiebreaker / next steps

Hi Sofia / Mark —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I've attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MedNex_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short evaluation plan (eval-plan-draft.pdf) that lays out acceptance criteria for latency, throughput, and security gating. High level:

- Customer ask: EU data residency and SOC2 evidence for audit next quarter.
- Decision point: Hosting mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) + which region(s) to run inference in for production.
- Proposed timeline:
  • Evaluation window: 2–3 weeks (pooled test traffic + perf e2e)
  • Decision & contract signature target: 2026-06-18
  • Go/no-go for production pilot: 2026-07-06

Two pragmatic options we've highlighted in the MAP:
1) Dedicated (EU region): predictable throughput, Redwood-managed capacity in eu-west, SLA-backed latency. Best fit if MedNex needs predictable peak capacity and wants Redwood to operate.
2) Private (on-prem / VPC): full data residency and control, longer lead time (infra + network), recommended if you require air-gapped processing or strict audit controls.

Hosted (global) remains an option for pilot traffic if you can accept a contractual data residency exception for the evaluation period — this reduces time-to-eval but is not recommended for long-term EU residency.

Next asks for you: please confirm whether the decision priority is (A) Residency first (Private/Dedicated in EU) or (B) Speed to evaluation (Hosted with data processing addenda for the pilot). I've flagged critical path items in the MAP and included a checklist for SOC2 artifacts in the data-residency-checklist.docx.

I'll follow-up internally to map availability for a Dedicated pool in eu-west and a timeline if you prefer Private.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment stubs: MedNex_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), eval-plan-draft.pdf (2 pages), data-residency-checklist.docx
From: Sofia Patel <sofia@mednex.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mark O'Connor <mark.oconnor@mednex.com>, DevOps Team <devops@mednex.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 11:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: Hosting mode & Region tiebreaker / next steps

Hi Camila —

Thank you, the MAP looks comprehensive. Quick answers from our side:

- Priority = Residency first. Our legal/compliance team is explicit that production inference for PHI-derived metadata must remain within the EU.
- We would like to evaluate Dedicated in eu-west as the primary path. Private (on-prem) is a fallback — we'd need an internal readiness check and longer procurement runway.

Two asks before we sign off on the MAP:
1) Can you share a high-level runbook for Dedicated onboarding (network peering, expected lead times, required IPs)?
2) For the evaluation, can Redwood guarantee a Dedicated pool with equivalent model/build as Hosted (same tokenizer, same quantization settings) so our perf tests are representative?

If you can confirm those two items by Friday (4 Jun), we can keep to your target decision date (18 Jun).

—Sofia
Sofia Patel
VP Product, MedNex Health
sofia@mednex.com
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Mutual Action Plan: Hosting mode & Region tiebreaker / next steps

Camila / Neha —

Looping in the technical ops notes I promised. Below are quick answers we can give MedNex and items we should own:

1) Dedicated onboarding runbook (summary):
   - Provisioning: allocate 2x A100-class nodes in eu-west for initial pilot (3–5 business days to schedule if capacity available; 10–14 days under heavy commit windows).
   - Network: we require a single peered subnet + BGP for egress IPs; provide expected IP ranges and firewall rules (I will draft these).
   - Model parity: Dedicated will run the same weights and quantization profile we test in Hosted. We will ship an identical container image and provide the same KV cache configuration.

2) Performance parity caveat: small differences possible due to instance types and NIC topology; we should include perf tolerances in the eval-plan (I suggest 5–10% token-latency buffer).

3) Private option: on-prem deployment requires SRE coordination — estimated 6–8 weeks from brief to first test unless MedNex pre-provisions hardware.

Action items for us to produce by Thu EOD (3 Jun):
- Lukas: dedicated-runbook-draft (network/IP/firewall + provisioning timeline)
- Neha: updated eval-plan with perf tolerances and test harness endpoints
- Camila: updated MAP with critical-path dates and contract checklist for Dedicated

If we can get those to Sofia by Friday, we keep their internal signoff cadence intact.

-Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Head of Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference
lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: Hosting mode & Region tiebreaker / next steps

Attached is the updated eval-plan-draft.pdf (v2) that includes:

- Test harness endpoints for Dedicated pilot (token-level latency, per-request throughput targets).
- Acceptance criteria: p95 latency <= 120ms for 4k context, 99% success rate, and end-to-end throughput >= 200 reqs/min for the canonical workload.
- Perf tolerance note: 5% buffer for Dedicated vs Hosted baseline.
- Data handling: confirmed that logs for Dedicated are retained per customer KMS; we added an export checklist for audit.

I'll also include a short-run perf test script (curl examples) in the Drive link.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Attachment stub: eval-plan-draft.pdf (v2)
From: Mark O'Connor <mark.oconnor@mednex.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Patel <sofia@mednex.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@mednex.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 16:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: Hosting mode & Region tiebreaker / next steps

Camila / team —

Appreciate the rapid turnaround. We reviewed the runbook summary and updated eval plan. MedNex confirms:

- We will proceed with Dedicated in eu-west for the production path.
- For the evaluation window we authorize Redwood to provision an isolated Dedicated pilot (pilot SLA to be included in the MAP).
- Legal requested a short statement of data residency controls (sample DPA clause + SOC2 artifacts) — if you can attach that to the MAP, we can include it in our procurement packet.

Decision note: Private/on-prem remains an option but is deprioritized given procurement timeline.

Next step for Redwood: please update the MAP with the Dedicated onboarding timeline and a one-page summary of data controls by Monday 8 Jun so our procurement can start paperwork.

Thanks,
Mark
Director of Infrastructure, MedNex Health
mark.oconnor@mednex.com
